newsitem.title: USA: Cargill reaches deal with North Korea for grain sale. [CORRECTED 21:35 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Cargill reaches deal with North Korea for grain sale. [CORRECTED 21:35 GMT]

text.p: The giant U.S. grain trader Cargill Inc. reached an agreement with the government of North Korea on Saturday to sell them an undisclosed amount of U.S. wheat, marking its first commercial sale of American grain to the communist regime (corrects to indicate not first U.S. sale ever, only with regard to Cargill).
"We have reached an agreement with the Democratic People's Republic of Korea for a commercial sale of U.S. wheat to be shipped in the near future," Cargill spokeswoman Lori Johnson said Monday.

The United States and South Korea launched a proposal a year ago for talks that would also bring in China to discuss a peace treaty formally ending the 1950-53 Korean war. U.S. and South Korean officials formally briefed North Korean diplomats on the idea in New York on March 5.

Burns said Pyongyang indicated it would respond soon when U.S. and North and South Korean diplomats met in New York last Friday. "Our hope, of course, is that the North Koreans will agree very soon to the four-party proposal themselves and that those talks can be begun," he said.

Asked about a statement by a South Korean foreign ministry spokesman on Monday that North Korea had asked for a second briefing, Burns said: "We've had a lot of briefings. We're willing to have another, I guess, but we'd really like the North Koreans to accept the proposal."

Meanwhile, the giant U.S. grain trader Cargill Inc. said it had reached an agreement with North Korea to sell it an undisclosed amount of U.S. wheat, marking the first commercial sale of American grain to the Communist regime. North Korea has been suffering from severe food shortages.
